name: Grilled Corn With Harissa and Smoked Paprika Butter

cookwares.name: charcoal briquettes and a chimney starter if using charcoal grill

instructions.primary_message: In a small bowl, combine the butter, lemon juice, paprika, harissa, garlic, honey, and salt. Season to taste with more salt or harissa.

Open bottom vent completely. Light large chimney starter filled 3/4 with charcoal briquettes (4 quarts). When top coals are partially covered with ash, pour evenly over bottom of grill. Set cooking grate in place, cover, and open lid vent completely. Heat grill until hot, about 5 minutes.
Turn all burners to high; cover; and heat grill until hot, about 15 minutes. Leave all burners on high.
Clean and oil cooking grate. Grill corn, turning frequently, until charred and tender on all sides, about 10 minutes.
Immediately slather corn with prepared harissa butter. Sprinkle with parsley and serve.

schema_metadata.keywords: Smoked Paprika, Harissa Butter, Grilled Corn, corn recipe, grilled corn recipe

description: Grilled corn is slathered with a harissa-spiked compound butter for a quick, flavorful side that's smoky, spicy, and perfect for summer.
notes:
Optional substitutions: harissa paste → more to taste

Notes: This recipe can easily be doubled.
For best results, look for a mild-to-medium-spicy harissa to balance heat without overpowering the other flavors. I recommend mild harissa and prefer the brand Mina.

Make-ahead and storage: The compound butter can be prepared ahead and refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 1 week.
author: Nargisse Benkabbou
